                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_conflict
              - text: between two
              - link "coalitions" [ref=f1e457] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coalition
              - text: ": the"
              - link "Allies" [ref=f1e458] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II
              - text: and the
              - link "Axis powers" [ref=f1e459] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axis_powers
              - text: .
              - link "Nearly all of the world's countries" [ref=f1e460] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II_by_country
              - text: participated, with many engaging in
              - link "total war" [ref=f1e461] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_war
              - text: on an unprecedented scale. World War II was the
              - link "deadliest conflict" [ref=f1e462] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_wars_by_death_toll
              - text: in history, causing the
              - link "deaths of 60 to 75 million people" [ref=f1e463] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II_casualties
              - text: ", a majority of whom were civilians. Millions died as a result of massacres, starvation, disease, and"
              - link "genocides" [ref=f1e464] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genocide
              - text: including
              - link "the Holocaust" [ref=f1e465] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Holocaust
              - text: . After the Allied victory,
              - link "Germany" [ref=f1e466] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allied-occupied_Germany
              - text: ","
              - link "Austria" [ref=f1e467] [cursor=pointer]:

              - link "Japanese" [ref=f1e471] [cursor=pointer]:

            - paragraph [ref=f1e532]:
              - text: World War II transformed the political, economic, and social structures of the world and established the foundation of international relations for the rest of the 20th century and into the 21st century. The United Nations was created to foster international cooperation and prevent future conflicts, with the victorious great powers—China, France, the Soviet Union, the United Kingdom, and the United States—becoming the
              - link "permanent members" [ref=f1e533] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permanent_members_of_the_United_Nations_Security_Council
              - text: of its
              - link "Security Council" [ref=f1e534] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_Council
              - text: . The Soviet Union and the United States emerged as rival superpowers, setting the stage for the
              - link "Cold War" [ref=f1e535] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War
              - text: . In the wake of Europe's devastation, the influence of its great powers waned, triggering the
              - link "decolonisation of Africa" [ref=f1e536] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decolonisation_of_Africa
              - text: and
              - link "of Asia" [ref=f1e537] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decolonisation_of_Asia
              - text: . Many countries whose industries had been damaged moved towards
              - link "economic recovery and expansion" [ref=f1e538] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post–World_War_II_economic_expansion
              - text: .

The most important factor accounting for the timing of surrender was the Soviet attack against Manchuria, largely because it persuaded previously adamant Army leaders that the homeland could not be defended\"."

[Between 1939 and 1945, approximately 200,000 women, men, and children from psychiatric institutions in the German Reich were murdered in several covert operations through gassing, drugging, or malnutrition. Nearly 100,000 additional murders of psychiatric patients occurred in occupied or annexed territories. Around one-third of the patient murders in the Reich took place during the so-called T4 program in its first, centrally directed phase.]
